issues.detail: The Hebrew 'לֹא יִהְיֶה כְלִי גֶבֶר עַל אִשָּׁה' means 'a man's attire shall not be on a woman' (i.e., a woman shall not wear a man's garment). The Chinese renders it as '男子的器皿不可屬於妻子' ('a man's vessel shall not belong to the wife'), which reverses the subject/object: it makes the man's item belong to the wife, whereas the Hebrew prohibits a woman from wearing a man's item. This changes who is doing what to whom.
